senses.gloss:
plu. only, m. (त्रयः) f. (तिस्रः) n. (त्रीणि)
Three.
subst. m. sing. (त्रिः) plu. (त्रयः)
Three times.
a.
thrice.
E.
तॄ to pass, Uṇādi affix क, and त्रि substituted.

mfn. (-शः-शा-शं)
Thirtieth.
E.
त्रिंशत, and ड aff.

mfn. (-कः-का-कं)
Thirty collectively, a multitude of thirty.
E.
त्रिंशत thirty, affix क्वुन्^1.
[1] Correction submitted by Jim Funderburk on 20161212. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/CORRECTIONS/issues/323, batches 309-312.

f. sing. (-त्)
Thirty, &c.
(-तौ)
Two thirties.
plu. (-तः)
Many thirties.
E.
त्रिं for त्रि three, and शत् aff.

n. (-त्रं)
The white esculent water lily.
E.
त्रिशत thirty, and पत्र a leaf.

n. (-कं)
1 The lower part of the spine.
2 The aggregate of three, a trine, a triad.
3 The three mystical words to be pronounced in daily prayer.
4 A place where three roads meet.
5 Three spices, three myrobalans, &c. collectively: see त्रिकटु, त्रिफल and the like.
m. (-कः)
A plant: see गोक्षुरक.
f. (-का)
1 A triangular frame or bar across the mouth of a well over which passes the rope of the bucket, or to which one end of it is tied to guard against, its slipping.
2 A wooden frame at the mouth of a well, or the upper part of the well.
3 A frame at the bottom of a well, on which the masonry rests.
4 The cover or lid of a well.
E.
त्रि three, and कन् aff.

m. (-द् or -त्)
A mountain with three peaks.
E.
त्रि, three, and ककुद a peak.

mfn. (-दः-दा-दं)
Having three humps or peaks.
E.
त्रि, and ककुद् a hump, and अच् aff.

m. (-टः)
A plant, (Ruellia longifolia,) &c. see गोक्षुरक.

m. (-टुः)
The aggregate of three spices, viz. black and long pepper, and dry ginger.
E.
त्रि three, or three-fold, and कटु pungent, (as a spice.)

m. (-ण्टः)
1 A plant, (Ruellia longifolia,) &c. त्रिकट.
2 A sort of Euphorbia.
E.
त्रि three, and कण्ट a thorn.

m. (-कः)
1 A sort of fish, (Silurus.)
2 A plant: see the preceding.
E.
कन् added to त्रिकण्ट.

m. (-यः)
A name of Buddha, the founder of the Bauddha sect.
E.
त्रि three, and काय a body, the three-bodied.

mfn. (-ज्ञः-ज्ञा-ज्ञं)
Omniscient.
m. (-ज्ञः)
1 A divine sage.
2 A deity.
3 A name of Buddha, the founder of the Bauddha sect^1.
E.
त्रि three, काल time, and ज्ञ who knows, acquainted with the past, present, and future; also similar compounds as the next, &c.
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210731. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/66.

mfn. (-शी-शिणी-शि)
Omniscient.
m. (-शी)
1 A Ṛṣi or divine sage.
2 A name of Buddha.
E.
त्रि three, काल time, and दर्शिन् who views: see the preceding.

mfn. (-विद्-वित्)
Omniscient.
m. (-विद् or -वित्)
A name of Buddha: see the preceding.
E.
as before, विद् who knows.

m. (-दः)
The name of a mountain in the peninsula; it is also applicable to any mountain with three peaks.
n. (-टं)
Sea salt prepared by evaporation.
E.
त्रि three, कूट a peak, &c.

n. (-कं)
A sort of knife with three edges.
E.
त्रि, and कूर्च्चक a bunch.

n. (-णं)
1 The vulva.
2 A triangle.
3 Any triangular object.
E.
त्रि three, and कोण a corner.

(इ) त्रिखि r. 1st cl. (त्रिङ्खति)
To go, to move or approach.

n. (-खं)
A cucumber.
E.
त्रि three, and ख a cavity or space; also read sometimes तृख.

nf. (-द्वं-द्वी)
The aggregate of three beds.
E.
त्रि three, खद्वा a bed, अच् aff.

m. (-णः)
The aggregate of three human objects, or virtue, wealth, and desire.
E.
त्रि three, and गण a class: see त्रिवर्ग.

mfn. (-तः-ता-तं)
1 Tripled.
2 Gone or done in three ways.
n. (-तं)
The expression of different senses by the same word.
E.
त्रि, and गत gone.

m. (-र्त्तः)
1 A country in the north-west division of India, or
m. plu. (-र्त्तः)
Its inhabitants: apparently part of Lahore, said, by Mr. WILFORD, to be the modern Tahora, but differently described in the Koṣas: see जालन्धर and वाह्लीक.
2 A form of calculation, (गणितान्तरे.)
f. (-र्त्ता)
1 A small worm.
2 A lascivious woman, a wanton.
3 A woman in general.
4 A pearl.
E.
त्रि three, and गर्त्त a hole, &c.

m. (-कः)
A country, the same as Vāhlika: see वाह्लीक.
E.
कन् added to the preceding.

mfn. (-णः-णा-णी-णं)
1 Thrice, three times, triple.
2 Possessing the three Guṇas or properties.
n. (-णं)
The aggregate of the three qualities incident to human nature.
E.
त्रि three, गुण a time or property.

mfn. (-तः-ता-तं)
Thrice ploughed, (a field, &c.)
E.
त्रिगुण three times, and आकृत made, wrought.

n. (-ढं)
The dancing or acting of a man in female attire.
E.
त्रि, and गूढ concealed.

mfn. plur. (-राः-राः-राणि)
Three or four.
E.
त्रि, and चतुर four, अच् added.

n. (-कं)
Three spices collectively, mace, cardamoms, and cassia leaf.
E.
त्रि, and जातक species.

f. (-ज्या)
A radius, a sine of three signs or ninety degrees.
E.
त्रि, and ज्या a sine.

n. (-णं)
Grass, meadow grass.
E.
see तृण, ऋ being changed to रि.

f. (-ता)
1 A bow.
2 The state or abstract property of grass.
E.
त्रिण for तृण grass, and तल् aff.

n. (-तं)
A portion of the Yajur Veda.
m. (-तः)
A follower of that branch of the Vedas. It is also sometimes read तृणाचिकेत.

nf. (-क्षः-क्षी)
An assemblage of three carpenters.
E.
त्रि three, तक्ष a carpenter, affix अण्.

mfn. (-यः-या-यं)
Third.
E.
त्रि three, तयप् aff.

n. (-ण्डं)
1 Three staves collectively.
2 Triple subjection of words, thoughts, and acts; the state of a religious ascetic.
E.
त्रि three, दण्ड a staff, &c.

n. (-णं)
Carrying three staves tied together, (as done by some mendicants.)
E.
त्रिदण्ड, and धारण holding.

m. (-ण्डी)
1 A wandering devotee, one who carries three long bambu staves in his right hand.
2 The religious man who has obtained a command over his words, thoughts, and actions, or mind, body, and speech.
E.
त्रि three, and दण्ड a punishment, a staff, &c. इनि aff.

f. (-ला)
A creeping plant, (Cissus pedata.)
E.
त्रि three, and दल a leaf.

m. (-शः)
A god, a deity, an immortal.
E.
त्रि the third, and दशा state, being, (youth); enjoying perpetual youth; or त्रि three, and दश state, subject as well as mortals to the three conditions, of birth, being, and destruction.

mfn. (-शः-शा-शं)
Thirteenth.
f. (-शी)
The thirteenth day of the fortnight; also त्रयोदश.

f. (-का)
The heavenly Ganges.
E.
त्रिदश a deity, and दीर्धिका a long pool.

mfn. plu. (-श)
Thirteen.
E.
त्रि three, and दशन् ten.

f. (-दी)
The heavenly Ganges.
E.
त्रिदश, and नदी a river.

m. (-तिः)
INDRA.
E.
त्रिदश, and पति chief.

f. (-धूः)
A nymph of INDRA'S heaven.
E.
त्रिदश, and बधू wife.

f. (-ता)
A nymph of INDRA'S heaven.
E.
त्रिदश, and वनिता a wife.

n. (-शं)
The thunderbolt.
E.
त्रिदश a deity, and अङ्कुश a goad.

m. (-र्य्यः)
The preceptor of the gods, VṚHASPATI.
E.
त्रिदश a deity, and आचार्य्य a teacher.

n. (-धं)
The thunderbolt of INDRA.
E.
त्रिदश a deity, and आयुध a weapon.

m. (-रिः)
An Asura or infernal being hostile to the gods, a Titan, a Giant.
E.
त्रिदश a deity, and अरि a foe.

m. (-यः)
1 Svarga, INDRA'S heaven or paradise.
2 The mountain Sumeru.
E.
त्रिदश a deity, and आलय an abode.

m. (-सः)
Svarga, the heaven of INDRA.
E.
त्रिदश a god, and आवास abode.

m. (-रः)
Amṛta or ambrosia.
E.
त्रिदश a deity, and आहार food.

f. (-का)
A plant, commonly Carmaghās.

n. (-नं)
Three days collectively.
E.
त्रि, and दिन a day.

m. (-स्पृक्)
Conjunction or concurrence of three lunations with one solar day.
E.
त्रिदिन, and स्पृश् contact.

mn. (-वः-वं)
1 Svarga or paradise.
2 Sky, atmosphere, heaven.
f. (-वा)
The name of a river.
E.
त्रि the three, BRAHMA, VIṢṆU, and ŚIVA, दिव to sport, affix क; the place where these three gods take divine pleasure.

m. (-शः)
A god, a deity.
E.
त्रिदिव heaven, and ईश master or lord.

m. (-काः)
A god, a celestial.
E.
त्रिदिव heaven, and ओकस् asylum.

mfn. (-दृक्)
Tri-ocular, three-eyed.
m. (-दृक्)
A name of ŚIVA.
E.
त्रि three, and दृश् an eye.

n. (-षं)
Disorder of the three humours of the body, vitiation of the bile, blood, and phlegm.
E.
त्रि three, and दोष a fault.

mfn. (-घ्नः-घ्नी-घ्नं)
Correcting the vitiated state of the three humours.
E.
त्रिदोष, and घ्न what destroys.

m. (-जः)
Disease, &c. proceeding from disorder of the three humours of the body
E.
त्रिदोष, and ज produced.

ind.
In three ways.
E.
त्रि, and धाच् aff.

m. (-तुः)
A name of GAṆEŚA.
n. (-तु)
Three minerals, &c.
E.
त्रि three, and धातु mineral, &c.

mfn. (-मा-मा-म)
Having three residences, &c.
m. (-मा)
1 A name of VIṢṆU.
2 An appellation of ŚIVA.
3 Agni or fire.
4 Death.
E.
त्रि three (worlds), and धामन् abode.

mfn. (-नः-नी-नं)
Three-eyed, tri-ocular.
m. (-नः)
A name of ŚIVA.
E.
त्रि three, and नयन an eye; this deity is represented with a third eye in his forehead; also similar compounds, as त्रिहृश्, त्रिनेत्र, त्र्यक्ष, &c.

mfn. (-त्रः-त्रा-त्रं)
Tri-ocular.
m. (-त्रः)
ŚIVA.
E.
त्रि, and नेत्र eye.

m. (-णिः)
The moon.
E.
त्रिनेत्र ŚIVA, त्रूडा a crest and मणि a gem; being worn by that deity as his crest.

n. (-क्षं)
A period of six weeks.
E.
त्रि, and पक्ष a fortnight.

m. (-कः)
1 The forehead marked naturally with three horizontal lines.
2 The hand with three fingers erect.
E.
त्रि three or three-fold, and पताका a banner, a symbol.

mfn. (-त्रः-त्रा-त्रं)
Three-leaved trefoil.
m. (-त्रः)
A fruit tree, (Ægle marmelos.)
E.
त्रि, and पत्र leaf.

m. (-कः)
The Kiṃśuka tree, (Butea frondosa.)
E.
त्रि three, and पत्र a leaf; having three leaves on each stalk.

n. (-थं)
1 A place where three roads meet.
2 Three ways or paths.
E.
त्रि, and पथ a road.

f. (-गा)
The Ganges.
E.
त्रिपथ three roads, and गा who goes, flowing through earth, heaven, and hell.

mfn. (-दः-दा-दी-दं)
1 Three-footed.
2 Having three lines or divisions, (a stanza.)
3 (In Arithmetic,) Trinomial.
n. (-दं)
1 A tripod.
f. (-दा)
A verse of three lines, as the Gāyatrī.
f. (-दी)
1 A creeper, (Cissus pedata.)
2 The girth of an elephant.
E.
त्रि three, and पद a foot.

mfn. (-र्णः-र्णी-र्णं)
Three-leaved trefoil.
f. (-र्णी)
Wild cotton.
E.
त्रि three, and पर्ण a leaf.

m. (-पाद्)
1 A name of VIṢṆU.
2 Fever, (personified.)
E.
त्रि three, and पाद foot or part; three-footed, alluding to VIṢṆU'S three steps which paced the universe; and the demon of fever is described in the Purāṇas, with three feet, and three heads, alluding probably to its three stages of cold, hot, and sweating.

m. (-वः)
A long-eared goat.
E.
त्रि, and पिव who drinks, touching water with both ears as he laps.

n. (-पं)
1 Heaven, Svarga or paradise.
2 Sky, æther.
E.
पिष्टप a world. and त्रि three, or the third; also त्रिविष्टप.

m. (-सद्)
A deity.
E.
त्रिपिष्टप heaven, and सद् who goes, from सद् with क्विप् affix; also त्रिविष्टपसद्.

m. (-टः)
1 Pulse, pease of three kinds.
2 A bank or shore.
3 A kind of vetch, (Cicer arietinum.)
4 A cubit.
5 A plant, (Ruellia longifolia.)
f. (-टा-टी)
A plant, (Convolvulus turpethum.)
f. (-टा)
Small cardamoms.
2 Arabian jasmine.
3 A goddess.
E.
त्रि three, and पुट skin or coat of a seed, &c.

m. (-कः)
A triangle.
E.
कन् added to the last.

m. (-टी)
The castor oil plant.
E.
त्रि three, पुट the seed vessel, and इनि aff.

m. (-लः)
The castor oil plant.
E.
त्रिपुटी as above, and फल fruit.

n. (-ण्ड्रं)
Three curved horizontal marks, made across the forehead with cowdung, ashes, &c.; they are worn especially by the followers of ŚIVA, or ŚAKTI, and are indispensable in proceeding to worship the former.
E.
त्रि three, triple, and पुण्ड्र a line; also with उन् added त्रिपुण्ड्रक.

n. (-कं)
See the preceding.

nf. (-रं-री)
A district, the modern Tipparah, &c.
m. (-रः)
The name of an Asura, and king of Tripura.
E.
त्रि three, and पुर a city, the district and dominion of that Asura, consisting of three strong and famous cities.

m. (-नः)
A name of ŚIVA.
E.
त्रिपुर the country of Tripura, and दहन burning, consuming; the Asura and his three cities being destroyed by MAHĀDEVA; also similar names, as त्रिपुरजित्, त्रिपुरसूदन, &c.

f. (-का)
A medicinal plant, apparently a kind of jasmine.
E.
त्रिपुर Tipperah, and मल्लिका jasmine.

m. (-कः)
A name of ŚIVA.
E.
त्रिपुर, and अन्तक ender, destroyer: see त्रिपुरदहन.

n. (-षं)
Three generations collectively.
E.
त्रि three, पुरुष a man.

mfn. (-तः-ता-तं)
Enjoyed or inherited through three generations.
E.
त्रिपुरुष, and आगत come.

mfn. (-षः-षी-षं)
Relating or belonging to three persons or generations, offered to three, (the funeral cake, &c.) inherited from three, (an estate, &c.)
E.
त्रिपुरुष, and अण् aff.

f. (-षा)
Black Tëori.

m. (-ष्ठः)
A king, and one of the Vāsudevas, or descendants of VASUDEVA, according to the Jains.

f. (-ला)
The three myrobalans.
E.
त्रि three, फल fruit, fem. affix टाप्; also with ङीष् affix त्रिफली.

n. (-कं)
The anus.
E.
त्रि three, (the three humors,) बुल to sink, affix कीकन्.

f. (-ण्डी)
A plant, (Convolvulus turpethum.)
E.
त्रि three, (ailments, or bile, phlegm, and fever,) भडि to oppose, affix अण् and ङीष्.

n. (-द्रं)
Copulation, cohabitation.
E.
त्रि three, and भद्र pleasurable.

m. (-जः)
A triangle.
E.
त्रि, and भुज an arm.

n. (-नं)
Three worlds, or heaven, earth, and hell.
E.
त्रि three, and भुवन a world.

m. (-धुः)
1 A portion of the Rig Veda.
2 A follower or student of the Tri-madhu section of the Rig Veda.
n. (-धुः)
Ghee, honey, and sugar.
E.
त्रि, and मधु honey.

f. (-र्ग्गी)
The meeting of three roads.
E.
त्रि three, and मार्ग्ग a road.

m. (-टः)
A mountain with three peaks.
E.
त्रि three, and मुकुट a crest.

mfn. (-खः-खी-खं)
Having three faces.
m. (-खः)
A divine attendant upon a Jaina saint.
f. (-खा)
A female deity of the Jaina sect.
E.
त्रि three, and मुख a face, three-faced, or त्रि three (worlds), and मुख principal.

m. (-र्त्तिः)
1 A Jina or Jaina saint.
2 The united form of BRAHMĀ, VIṢṆU, and ŚIVA, or the Hindu trial.
3 One possessing three forms or modes of being.
E.
त्रि three, and मूर्त्ति form, matter.

mfn. (-र्द्धः-र्द्धी-र्द्धं)
Three-headed.
E.
त्रि, and मूर्द्धन् the forehead, ष aff.

n. (-बः)
A Ratti or weight of three barley-corns.
E.
त्रि, and यव barley.

m. (-ष्टिः)
A medicinal plant, (Mollugo pentaphylla.)
E.
त्रि three, and यष्टि a line; having three stalks.

n. (-कं)
Sin.
E.
स्त्रि the three objects of life, and यामक impeder, from यम, with ण्वुल् aff.

f. (-मा)
1 Night.
2 The YAMUNĀ or Jumna river.
3 Indigo.
4 Black Tëori, a plant so called.
E.
त्रि three (times, or past, present, and future,) या to go, affix मन्.

m. (-हः)
A brown or chesnut horse.

n. (-त्रं)
Three nights collectively, or the duration of three nights.
E.
त्रि three, and रात्रि a night; compounded with a numeral रात्रि substitutes अ for its final, and becomes neuter.

m. (-खः)
A conch.
E.
त्रि, and रेखा a line; this shell being marked with three lines.

f. (-की)
The aggregate of the three worlds, or heaven, earth, and hell, collectively.
E.
त्रि three, and लोक a world, and ङीप् affix, with the sense of aggregation.

m. (-शः)
The sun.
E.
त्रिलोक the three worlds or the universe, and ईश lord.

mfn. (-नः-नी-नं)
Tri-ocular, three-eyed.
m. (-नः)
A name of ŚIVA.
f. (-ना)
A female deity of the Jainas.
f. (-नी)
A name of DURGĀ.
E.
त्रि three, and लोचन an eye: see त्रिदृश् &c.

n. (-कं)
Gold, silver, and copper.
E.
त्रि, and लोहक metal.

m. (-र्गः)
1 Three human objects or pursuits, as love, duty, and wealth.
2 Three conditions of a king or state; prosperity, evenness, and decay; or loss, gain, equality, &c.
3 The three qualities of nature, purity, blindness, and depravity.
4 The three myrobalans.
5 The three spices: see त्रिकटु.
6 Propriety, good behaviour.
E.
त्रि three, and वर्ग a class; a class or aggregate of three.

mfn. (-णः-णा-णं)
Having passed through the three conditions, or attained the three objects of life.
E.
त्रिवर्ग, and पारीण gone to the opposite shore.

n. (-कं)
1 The three myrobalans.
2 The three spices.
3 A plant, (Ruellia longifolia): see गोक्षुरक.
E.
त्रि three, वर्ण a class, and कन् added.

f. (-का)
A three years old heifer.
E.
त्रि, and वर्ष a year, affix ठन्.

f. (-ली)
Three folds of skin on the abdomen, from obesity.
E.
त्रि, and वली a wrinkle.

m. (-मः)
A name of VIṢṆU.
E.
त्रि, and विक्रम going; crossing over the three worlds in three steps, to the discomfiture of BĀLĪ.

f. (-द्या)
Three branches of knowledge, especially that of the three Vedas.
E.
त्रि, and विद्या knowledge.

mfn. (-धः-धा-धं)
In three ways, of three kinds.
E.
त्रि, and विध sort.

n. (-पं)
1 Heaven or paradise.
2 The three worlds, or heaven, earth, and hell: see त्रिपिष्टप.

m. (-सद)
A deity; also त्रिपिष्टपसद्.

mfn. (-वृत्)
Triple, tri-form, three-fold.
m. (-वृत्)
1 A plant of valuable purgative properties, commonly called Tëori, and distinguished into two species, white and black, (Convolvulus turpethum.)
2 Combining any thing by three.
2 A triple cord, a girdle, &c. of three strings.
3 A kind of sacrifice.
E.
त्रि three, (three seed vessels,) वृ to cherish, affix क्विप्, and तुक् added; also with टाप् added त्रिवृता (-ता.)

n. (-णं)
Combining earth, water, and fire, in the proportion of half of one with a quarter of each of the others.
E.
त्रिवृत्, and करण making.

f. (-र्णी)
A potherb, (Hilancha repens.)
E.
त्रिवृत् Tëori, and पर्ण a leaf; having similar leaves.

f. (-णी)
A name of the Ganges.
E.
त्रि three, वेणी a braid of hair: the name is especially applied to the river at Allahabad, where it receives the Jumna, and is supposed to receive under ground the Sarasvatī; it is also that of a village in Bengal, above Hugli.

n. (-दं)
The three Vedas collectively.
E.
त्रि, and वेद a Veda.

m. (-दी)
A Brahman acquainted with three Vedas.
E.
त्रिवेद्, and इनि aff.

m. (ङ्कुः)
1 The name of a king of the solar race, famous for attempting to go to heaven in his mortal frame, by the aid of VIŚVĀMITRA.
2 A cat.
3 A grasshopper.
4 A bird, the Cātaka, (Cuculus melanoleucos.)
5 A fire-fly.
E.
त्रि three, शङ्कु a dart, ट aff.

m. (-जः)
A name of HARIŚCANDRA, a prince.
E.
त्रिशङ्कु, and ज born, descended from TRIŚAṄKU.

m. (-जी)
VIŚVĀMITRA, a celebrated sage and saint.
E.
त्रिशङ्कु the king so named, and याजिन् causing to worship; being the family priest of the monarch.

m. (-णः)
A Jina, a sanctified teacher of the Jaina sect.
E.
त्रि three, (the three worlds,) and शरण protection.

f. (-ला)
The mother of VARDDHAMĀNA, the last of the Jaina pontiffs.

mfn. (-खः-खा-खं)
Three-crested, three-headed.
n. (-खं)
1 A crest, a tiara with three points.
2 A trident, a three-pronged spear.
m. (-खः)
The son of RĀVAṆA, a demon with three heads.
E.
त्रि three, and शिखा a crest.

mfn. (-राः-राः-रः)
Three-headed.
m. (-राः)
A name of KUVERA.
2 Fever personified as a demon with three heads: see त्रिपाद.
3 A son of RĀVAṆA.
E.
त्रि three, and शिरस् a head.

mfn. (-कः-का-कं)
Three-headed.
m. (-कः)
A trident, a tri-pointed spear.
E.
त्रि three, and शीर्ष a head, affix कन्.

n. (-लं)
A trident, a three-pointed pike or spear, especially the weapon of ŚIVA.
E.
त्रि three or Tri, and शूल a dart.

m. (-ली)
A name of ŚIVA.
E.
त्रिशूल, and इनि affix, armed with a trident.

m. (-ङ्गः).
1 A hill with three peaks.
2 A triangle.
E.
त्रि three, and शृङ्ग a horn.

m. (-ङ्गी)
A sort of fish, commonly^1 Rohi, (Cyprinus rohita, HAM.)
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210731. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/66.

n. (-णं)
The three ablutions to be performed in the day, or at dawn, noon, and sun-set.
E.
त्रि three, सवन bathing; also read त्रिसवन.

m. (-यी)
A man performing regularly the prescribed ablutions, morning, noon, and night.
E.
त्रि three, सवन time or period of ablution, and स्नायिन् who bathes.

f. (-ष्टुप्)
A form of metre, the stanza consisting of four lines of eleven syllables each, or of five lines, one of eleven [] and four of eight each, forming altogether forty-four syllables; there are other varieties.

mfn. (-ष्ठः-ष्ठा-ष्ठं)
Situated in three places.
E.
त्रि, and स्था to be, क aff.

mfn. (-न्ध्यः-न्ध्या or -न्ध्यी-न्ध्यं)
The three periods of the day, or dawn, noon, and eve.
E.
त्रि three, and सन्ध्य either of the periods.

n. (-मं)
An aggregate of three like or equal things.
E.
त्रि, and सम same.

subst. mfn. (-रः-रा-रं)
A dish of sesamum, rice, &c.
E.
त्रि three, three-fold, and सर what is, from सृ to go or get, affix अप्.

n. (-नं)
Bathing thrice: see त्रिषवण.

mfn. (-त्यः-त्या-त्यं)
Thrice ploughed, (a field, &c.)
E.
त्रि thrice, and सीत्य ploughed.

m. (-र्णः)
1 A portion of the Rig and Yajur Vedas.
2 An observance enjoined by it.
2 A Brahman following it.

m. (-कः)
A Tri Suparṇa Brahman: see the last.

f. (-ताः)
1 The Ganges.
2 Another river.
E.
त्रि three, and स्रोतस् a river, the river of the three worlds, or one with three channels.

mfn. (-ल्यः-ल्या-ल्यं)
Thrice ploughed, (a field, &c.)
E.
त्रि thrice, हल्य ploughed.

mfn. (-णः-णी-णं)
Three years, (old, &c.)
f. (-णी)
A threeyears-old heifer.
E.
त्रि, and हायन a year; also read त्रिहायन.
